answer: Instead of counting wallets, the protocol prices identity by sequential, peer-replayable labor. A newcomer posts slashable collateral as its anchor, then must complete a ladder of tiny jobs whose outputs are lashed to a public trellis of height-stamped hashes signed by already-established graders. Only when that lineage is dense and collision-free does the ledger mint one non-transferable pearl of voting weight bound to the original key. A farm that clones keys cannot split the pearl, and reused traces slash the collateral, so extra identities purchase delay and loss rather than extra ballots.
